claim: TRPV5 is a highly calcium selective ion channel that acts as the rate-limiting step of calcium reabsorption in the kidney.
source: Transient receptor potential vanilloid 5 (TRPV5) is a highly calcium selective ion channel that acts as the rate-limiting step of calcium reabsorption in the kidney.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that is supported by established scientific knowledge about TRPV5 function.

claim: The lack of potent, specific modulators of TRPV5 has limited the ability to probe the contribution of TRPV5 in disease phenotypes such as hypercalcemia and nephrolithiasis.
source: The lack of potent, specific modulators of TRPV5 has limited the ability to probe the contribution of TRPV5 in disease phenotypes such as hypercalcemia and nephrolithiasis.
evidence: This statement is supported by inference from the current state of research and the need for better tools.

claim: Structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) at a previously identified TRPV5 inhibitor binding site coupled with electrophysiology screening identified three novel inhibitors of TRPV5.
source: Here, we performed structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) at a previously identified TRPV5 inhibitor binding site coupled with electrophysiology screening and identified three novel inhibitors of TRPV5, one of which exhibits high affinity, and specificity for TRPV5 over other TRP channels, including its close homologue TRPV6.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript, including virtual screening results and electrophysiology experiments.

claim: One of the three novel inhibitors exhibits high affinity and specificity for TRPV5 over other TRP channels, including its close homologue TRPV6.
source: Here, we performed structure-based virtual screening (SBVS) at a previously identified TRPV5 inhibitor binding site coupled with electrophysiology screening and identified three novel inhibitors of TRPV5, one of which exhibits high affinity, and specificity for TRPV5 over other TRP channels, including its close homologue TRPV6.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing IC50 values and selectivity testing across multiple TRP channels.

claim: Cryo-electron microscopy of TRPV5 in the presence of the specific inhibitor and its parent compound revealed novel binding sites for this channel.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy of TRPV5 in the presence of the specific inhibitor and its parent compound revealed novel binding sites for this channel.
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structures presented in the manuscript showing inhibitor densities at specific locations.

claim: TRPV5 is responsible for the fine tuning of calcium reabsorption in the kidney and has been shown to be a critical component of systemic calcium homeostasis.
source: TRPV5 is a calcium selective ion channel that is responsible for the fine tuning of calcium reabsorption in the kidney and has been shown to be a critical component of systemic calcium homeostasis (Peng et al., 2000; Hoenderop et al., 2003; de Groot et al., 2008; Na and Peng, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Potent and specific chemical modulators of TRPV5 have the potential to aid in treatments of calcium homeostasis disorders such as nephrolithiasis and hypercalcemia.
source: Due to its role in calcium handling, potent and specific chemical modulators of TRPV5 have the potential to aid in treatments of calcium homeostasis disorders such as nephrolithiasis and hypercalcemia (Nie et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents speculation about potential therapeutic applications.

claim: Econazole, TH-1177, and select cannabinoids are synthetic modulators of TRPV5 with reported potencies in the mid-micromolar range.
source: While there are some synthetic modulators of TRPV5 including econazole (Nilius et al., 2001; Hughes et al., 2018a), TH-1177 (Landowski et al., 2011; Peng et al., 2018), and select cannabinoids (Janssens et al., 2018), all have reported potencies in the mid-micromolar range and currently none have robust selectivity for TRPV5 over TRPV6 and the other TRPV subfamily channels (Nilius et al., 2001; Landowski et al., 2011; Peng et al., 2018; Janssens et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Currently available synthetic modulators of TRPV5 lack robust selectivity for TRPV5 over TRPV6 and other TRPV subfamily channels.
source: While there are some synthetic modulators of TRPV5 including econazole (Nilius et al., 2001; Hughes et al., 2018a), TH-1177 (Landowski et al., 2011; Peng et al., 2018), and select cannabinoids (Janssens et al., 2018), all have reported potencies in the mid-micromolar range and currently none have robust selectivity for TRPV5 over TRPV6 and the other TRPV subfamily channels (Nilius et al., 2001; Landowski et al., 2011; Peng et al., 2018; Janssens et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Binding of PI(4,5)P2 is critical for TRPV5 channel opening.
source: In the cell, binding of PI(4,5)P2 is critical for channel opening while rapid desensitization occurs via binding of calmodulin (CaM) to the base of the pore (Na and Peng, 2014; Hughes et al., 2018a; van der Wijst et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Rapid desensitization of TRPV5 occurs via binding of calmodulin (CaM) to the base of the pore.
source: In the cell, binding of PI(4,5)P2 is critical for channel opening while rapid desensitization occurs via binding of calmodulin (CaM) to the base of the pore (Na and Peng, 2014; Hughes et al., 2018a; van der Wijst et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Allosteric modulators are more likely to be both potent and specific for TRPV5 due to the conserved nature of PI(4,5)P2 modulation within the TRP channel family.
source: Due to the conserved nature of PI(4,5)P2 modulation within the TRP channel family, allosteric modulators are more likely to be both potent and specific for TRPV5 (Rohács et al., 2005; Thyagarajan et al., 2008; Rohacs, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and represents an inference about drug design strategy.

claim: The econazole-binding pocket of TRPV5 was reported in the same location as the vanilloid binding pocket in TRPV1.
source: Here, we screened the previously identified econazole-binding pocket of TRPV5 (Hughes et al., 2018b), which was reported in the same location as the vanilloid binding pocket in TRPV1 (Hughes et al., 2018b; Gao et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The allosteric binding site in TRPV5 has been reported to bind modulators such as small molecules and lipids in several TRPV subfamily channels.
source: This allosteric binding site has been reported to bind modulators such as small molecules and lipids in several TRPV subfamily channels (Hughes et al., 2018a; Hughes et al., 2018b; Gao et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Three novel synthetic inhibitors of TRPV5 have not been previously characterized as modulators for any protein.
source: Through this screen we identified three novel synthetic inhibitors that to our best knowledge have not been previously characterized as modulators for any protein.
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' knowledge of the literature and represents a novelty claim.

claim: The econazole-bound TRPV5 structure revealed that econazole bound in the 'vanilloid' pocket of TRPV5.
source: The econazole-bound TRPV5 structure revealed that the small-molecule inhibitor of TRPV5, econazole, bound in the 'vanilloid' pocket of TRPV5, which is a well-documented site of modulator binding in other TRPV channels (Hughes et al., 2018b; Gao et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The vanilloid pocket is a well-documented site of modulator binding in other TRPV channels.
source: The econazole-bound TRPV5 structure revealed that the small-molecule inhibitor of TRPV5, econazole, bound in the 'vanilloid' pocket of TRPV5, which is a well-documented site of modulator binding in other TRPV channels (Hughes et al., 2018b; Gao et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The binding pocket used for SBVS is located at the interface of two adjacent monomers and is composed of the S3, S4 and S4-S5 linker of one monomer and the S5 and S6 helices of the second monomer.
source: Specifically, this binding pocket is located at the interface of two adjacent monomers and is composed of the S3, S4 and S4-S5 linker of one monomer and the S5 and S6 helices of the second monomer (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data and reference to a figure.

claim: The lipid-bound TRPV5 structure allowed for unambiguous backbone placement and confident side chain placement in the binding pocket.
source: The resolution of this pocket in the lipid-bound TRPV5 structure allowed for unambiguous backbone placement and confident side chain placement.
evidence: This claim is based on the quality of the structural data obtained.

claim: Approximately 12 million compounds from the ZINC15 'Drugs Now' library were docked into the TRPV5 binding pocket.
source: Using the Schrodinger suite 2018–1,~12 million compounds from the ZINC15 'Drugs Now' library, were docked into this pocket.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method used.

claim: The top 100 compounds from the virtual screen were grouped into 65 clusters of unique chemical scaffolds based on their chemical similarity.
source: The top 100 compounds as ranked by their docking score were grouped into 65 clusters of unique chemical scaffolds based on their chemical similarity assessed by Tanimoto similarity scores of ECFP4 binary fingerprints (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a description of the data analysis method used.

claim: Econazole was not part of the 'in stock' library and was therefore excluded from the original screen.
source: Econazole was not part of the 'in stock' library and was therefore excluded from the original screen.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental design.

claim: A follow up screen that included econazole revealed a less favorable docking score (−5.9) compared to the top 100 hits (<−9.0).
source: A follow up screen in the same pocket that included econazole revealed a less favorable docking score (−5.9) compared to the top 100 hits (<−9.0).
evidence: This is experimental data from the virtual screening.

claim: None of the top 100 compounds exhibited significant similarity with econazole or other known TRPV5 inhibitors.
source: Additionally, none of these top 100 compounds exhibited significant similarity (defined by a Tanimoto similarity score larger than 0.4) with econazole or other known TRPV5 inhibitors.
evidence: This is an analysis of the virtual screening results.

claim: 43 compounds were purchased based on availability and price from the 65 unique chemical scaffolds identified.
source: Of the 65 unique chemical scaffolds identified as cluster representatives (centroid of clusters), 43 compounds were purchased based on availability and price (Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure.

claim: TRPV5 conducts monovalent currents in the absence of Ca2+ and Mg2+.
source: While TRPV5 is a Ca2+ selective ion channel, it conducts monovalent currents in the absence of Ca2+ and Mg2+.
evidence: This is established knowledge about TRPV5 channel properties.

claim: Monovalent currents through TRPV5 are routinely used for assessing channel function because Ca2+ currents are smaller and undergo Ca2+-induced inactivation.
source: Ca2+ currents are not only smaller than monovalent currents, but they also undergo Ca2+-induced inactivation, therefore monovalent currents are routinely used for assessing channel function (Hoenderop et al., 2001; Velisetty et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research describing experimental methods.

claim: 41 of the 43 tested compounds showed no clear inhibition or potentiation of TRPV5 currents.
source: Each compound was tested at 10 μM or 3 μM and 41 of them showed no clear inhibition or potentiation of TRPV5 currents (Figure 1—source data 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is experimental data from the electrophysiology screening.

claim: Two of the 43 screened compounds measurably inhibited TRPV5-mediated currents.
source: Two of the 43 screened compounds measurably inhibited TRPV5-mediated currents in our system.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the electrophysiology experiments.

claim: ZINC9155420 showed robust (~80%) inhibition of rabbit TRPV5 at 10 µM.
source: One of the hit compounds, ZINC9155420 showed robust (~80%) inhibition of rabbit TRPV5 at 10 µM, and did not appear to have any selectivity for TRPV5 over the closely related TRPV6 channel (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is experimental data from patch clamp experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: ZINC9155420 did not appear to have any selectivity for TRPV5 over the closely related TRPV6 channel.
source: One of the hit compounds, ZINC9155420 showed robust (~80%) inhibition of rabbit TRPV5 at 10 µM, and did not appear to have any selectivity for TRPV5 over the closely related TRPV6 channel (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is experimental data from patch clamp experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: The IC50 of ZINC9155420 for rbTRPV5 inhibition in HEK293 cells was 2.91 ± 0.56 µM.
source: In HEK293 cells, the IC50 of ZINC9155420 for rbTRPV5 inhibition was 2.91 ± 0.56 µM, which is of comparable potency to econazole (Nilius et al., 2001; Hughes et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is experimental data from dose-response experiments.

claim: ZINC9155420 has comparable potency to econazole for TRPV5 inhibition.
source: In HEK293 cells, the IC50 of ZINC9155420 for rbTRPV5 inhibition was 2.91 ± 0.56 µM, which is of comparable potency to econazole (Nilius et al., 2001; Hughes et al., 2018b).
evidence: This claim compares experimental data to previously published results cited in the text.

claim: ZINC9155420 inhibited hTRPV6 channel with an IC50 of 4.05 ± 1.04 μM in HEK293 cells.
source: This compound also inhibited the hTRPV6 channel with a comparable IC50 in the same system (4.05 ± 1.04 μM, Figure 1C).
evidence: This is experimental data from dose-response experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Five chemical analogs of ZINC9155420 were purchased based on vendor availability and price.
source: Five chemical analogs of ZINC9155420 were purchased based on vendor availability and price.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental procedure.

claim: Four of the five derivatives of ZINC9155420 showed no effect on TRPV5 activity.
source: These compounds were tested in the HEK293 cell expression system and four of these derivatives showed no effect on TRPV5 activity (Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This is experimental data from the electrophysiology screening.

claim: ZINC17988990 was found to be a potent inhibitor of TRPV5 mediated currents.
source: The fifth derivative, ZINC17988990, was found to be a potent inhibitor of TRPV5 mediated currents.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the electrophysiology experiments.

claim: ZINC17988990 exhibited robust inhibition of rbTRPV5 with an IC50 of 106 ± 27 nM.
source: This compound exhibited robust inhibition of rbTRPV5 with an IC50 of 106 ± 27 nM while also showing marked selectivity for TRPV5 over TRPV6 (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is experimental data from dose-response experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: ZINC17988990 showed marked selectivity for TRPV5 over TRPV6.
source: This compound exhibited robust inhibition of rbTRPV5 with an IC50 of 106 ± 27 nM while also showing marked selectivity for TRPV5 over TRPV6 (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is experimental data from selectivity testing shown in Figure 1.

claim: Human TRPV6 was not inhibited by ZINC17988990 at concentrations up to 10 µM in HEK293 cells.
source: Human TRPV6 was not inhibited by ZINC17988990 at concentrations up to 10 µM in the same system (Figure 1E–F).
evidence: This is experimental data from patch clamp experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: ZINC17988990 had no activity on TRPV1, TRPV3, TRPV4 and TRPM8 at low concentrations (1–3 µM).
source: Additionally, ZINC17988990 had no activity on other TRP channels tested (TRPV1, TRPV3, TRPV4 and TRPM8) at low concentrations (1–3 µM), but did exhibit moderate inhibition on TRPV3 and TRPM8 at concentrations above 10 µM (Figure 2).
evidence: This is experimental data from selectivity testing shown in Figure 2.

claim: ZINC17988990 exhibited moderate inhibition on TRPV3 and TRPM8 at concentrations above 10 µM.
source: Additionally, ZINC17988990 had no activity on other TRP channels tested (TRPV1, TRPV3, TRPV4 and TRPM8) at low concentrations (1–3 µM), but did exhibit moderate inhibition on TRPV3 and TRPM8 at concentrations above 10 µM (Figure 2).
evidence: This is experimental data from selectivity testing shown in Figure 2.

claim: ZINC17988990 has comparable inhibition of the human isoform of TRPV5 with an IC50 of 177 ± 47 nM.
source: Further characterization of ZINC17988990 revealed that it has comparable inhibition of the human isoform of TRPV5 (IC50 = 177 ± 47 nM, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is experimental data from dose-response experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nanodisc-reconstituted TRPV5 in the presence of 10 µM ZINC9155420 was resolved to 4.3 Å by cryo-EM.
source: We were able to resolve nanodisc-reconstituted TRPV5 in the presence of 10 µM ZINC9155420 or ZINC17988990 to 4.3 Å and 3.8 Å, respectively (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplements 1–4, Table 1).
evidence: This is structural data from cryo-EM experiments.

claim: Nanodisc-reconstituted TRPV5 in the presence of 10 µM ZINC17988990 was resolved to 3.8 Å by cryo-EM.
source: We were able to resolve nanodisc-reconstituted TRPV5 in the presence of 10 µM ZINC9155420 or ZINC17988990 to 4.3 Å and 3.8 Å, respectively (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplements 1–4, Table 1).
evidence: This is structural data from cryo-EM experiments.

claim: The inhibitor-bound TRPV5 structures are consistent with the architecture of previously reported structures of TRPV5.
source: These structures are consistent with the architecture of the previously reported structures of TRPV5 (Hughes et al., 2018a; Hughes et al., 2018b; Dang et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim compares the new structures to previously published structures cited in the text.

claim: The transmembrane domain (TMD) of TRPV5 consists of transmembrane helices 1–4 (S1-S4) bundled in a voltage sensing-like domain with helices 5 and 6 (S5 and S6) domain swapped to create the pore of the channel.
source: The transmembrane domain (TMD) consists of transmembrane helices 1–4 (S1-S4) bundled in a voltage sensing-like domain with helices 5 and 6 (S5 and S6) domain swapped to create the pore of the channel.
evidence: This is a description of the structural architecture observed in the cryo-EM structures.

claim: The intracellular portion of TRPV5 is primarily composed of tightly packed ankyrin repeat domains (ARDs).
source: The intracellular portion of the protein is primarily composed of tightly packed ankyrin repeat domains (ARDs).
evidence: This is a description of the structural architecture observed in the cryo-EM structures.

claim: Higher local resolution in the TMD of both inhibitor-bound structures allowed for confident placement of side chains.
source: Higher local resolution in the TMD of both structures allowed for the confident placement of side chains in this region when building the model (Figure 3—figure supplements 1–4).
evidence: This is a statement about the quality of the structural data.

claim: The ion conduction pathway for both inhibitor-bound structures are in non-conducting conformations.
source: At these resolutions, we were able to clearly identify that the ion conduction pathway for both inhibitor-bound structures are in non-conducting conformations (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is an analysis of the structural data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5.

claim: Non-protein densities in the TMD of both inhibitor-bound structures were attributed to bound inhibitors.
source: We were also able to identify at these resolutions non-protein densities in the TMD of both structures that we attributed to bound inhibitors (Figure 3).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cryo-EM density maps shown in Figure 3.

claim: The ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure revealed two densities that could be attributed to bound compounds.
source: The ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure revealed two densities that could be attributed to bound compounds (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3.

claim: One density identified in the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure is located between the intracellular S1-S4 bundle and the TRP helix.
source: One density identified in the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure is located between the intracellular S1-S4 bundle and the TRP helix and it is present in the sharpened map as well as both of the half-maps (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 4.

claim: The S1-S4 bundle in the ZINC17988990-bound structure was resolved to a local resolution of 3.0–3.5 Å.
source: This S1-S4 bundle was resolved in this structure to a local resolution of 3.0–3.5 Å which allowed for confident backbone and side chain placement (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a statement about the quality of the structural data.

claim: The upper region of the S1-S4 pocket has been consistently occupied by lipids in previous TRPV5 channel structures.
source: Though the upper region of the S1-S4 pocket has been consistently occupied by lipids in the previous TRPV5 channel structures (Hughes et al., 2018a; Hughes et al., 2018b; Dang et al., 2019), a density lower in the pocket has been identified for the first time in the ZINC17988990-bound structure (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim compares the new structure to previously published structures cited in the text.

claim: A density lower in the S1-S4 pocket has been identified for the first time in the ZINC17988990-bound structure.
source: Though the upper region of the S1-S4 pocket has been consistently occupied by lipids in the previous TRPV5 channel structures (Hughes et al., 2018a; Hughes et al., 2018b; Dang et al., 2019), a density lower in the pocket has been identified for the first time in the ZINC17988990-bound structure (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a novel observation from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: In cryo-EM structures of TRPM8 and TRPV6, densities attributed to small-molecule modulators were identified in the S1-S4 pocket.
source: In cryo-EM structures of other TRP channels, such as TRPM8 and TRPV6, densities attributed to small-molecule modulators were also identified in this S1-S4 pocket (Figure 4—figure supplement 2)(Yin et al., 2019; Singh et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies and reference to a figure.

claim: In TRPV6, small-molecule modulator binding in the S1-S4 pocket was proposed despite lipid binding reported in the same area in previous structures.
source: In the case of TRPV6, this was proposed in spite of lipid binding reported in the same area in previous structures (Singh et al., 2018; McGoldrick et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The absence of the lower density in previously published TRPV5 cryo-EM structures led to attributing this density to bound ZINC17988990.
source: This precedent, along with the absence of the lower density in previously published TRPV5 cryo-EM structures (Hughes et al., 2018a; Hughes et al., 2018b; Dang et al., 2019), has led us to attribute this density to bound ZINC17988990.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison to previous structures and precedent from other TRP channels.

claim: The residues that constitute the S1-S4 bundle binding site in the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure include E403, D406, Y415, Y467 and F468.
source: The residues that constitute this binding site in the S1-S4 bundle of the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure include E403, D406, Y415, Y467 and F468 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Of the residues that contact the compound density in the EM map, only Y415 is not conserved between TRPV5 and TRPV6.
source: Of these residues that contact the compound density in the EM map, only Y415 is not conserved between TRPV5 and TRPV6 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is an analysis of sequence conservation shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A.

claim: In TRPV6, the residue at position Y415 (TRPV5 numbering) is a phenylalanine.
source: In TRPV6, the residue at this position is a phenylalanine.
evidence: This is a statement about sequence conservation based on sequence alignment.

claim: The F468A mutation of TRPV5 created a non-functional channel.
source: The F468A mutation created a non-functional channel, implying this residue is important for proper protein folding, trafficking to the membrane and/or activation by PI(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is experimental data from mutagenesis experiments.

claim: F468 is important for proper protein folding, trafficking to the membrane and/or activation by PI(4,5)P2.
source: The F468A mutation created a non-functional channel, implying this residue is important for proper protein folding, trafficking to the membrane and/or activation by PI(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental observation that F468A is non-functional.

claim: The D406A mutation eliminated inhibition of TRPV5 by ZINC17988990 at low concentrations while maintaining the inhibitory effect at higher concentrations, resulting in an IC50 of 3.68 ± 1.03 μM.
source: The D406A mutation eliminated inhibition of the channel at low concentrations while maintaining the inhibitory effect at higher concentrations, resulting in an IC50 of 3.68 ± 1.03 μM.
evidence: This is experimental data from mutagenesis and dose-response experiments.

claim: The Y415F mutation resulted in a reduced potency of ZINC17988990, resulting in an IC50 of 0.644 ± 0.106 μM.
source: The Y415F mutation also resulted in a reduced potency of ZINC17988990, resulting in an IC50 of 0.644 ± 0.106 μM (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is experimental data from mutagenesis and dose-response experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The substantially reduced inhibitory effects of S1-S4 bundle mutant channels indicate that ZINC17988990 exerts its inhibitory effect primarily by binding in this pocket.
source: The substantially reduced inhibitory effects of these S1-S4 bundle mutant channels indicate that this compound exerts its inhibitory effect primarily by binding in this pocket.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutagenesis data.

claim: The D406A mutant did not reduce inhibition of TRPV5 by ZINC9155420.
source: The D406A mutant did not reduce inhibition of TRPV5 by ZINC9155420, which appears to bind in a different area of the TMD (Figure 3A–B; also see following section), indeed this mutant required slightly lower concentrations of the drug than wild type (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is experimental data from mutagenesis experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: ZINC9155420 appears to bind in a different area of the TMD than ZINC17988990.
source: The D406A mutant did not reduce inhibition of TRPV5 by ZINC9155420, which appears to bind in a different area of the TMD (Figure 3A–B; also see following section), indeed this mutant required slightly lower concentrations of the drug than wild type (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutagenesis data and structural observations.

claim: The D406A mutant did not reduce inhibition by ZINC17988990 non-specifically by increasing open state stability of the channel, but rather by specifically interfering with drug binding.
source: This indicates that the D406A mutant did not reduce inhibition by ZINC17988990 non-specifically by increasing open state stability of the channel, but rather by specifically interfering drug binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of D406A on ZINC17988990 vs ZINC9155420.

claim: The second density in the ZINC17988990-bound structure appeared to be bound at the interface of the S4-S5 linker of one monomer and the S6 helix of an adjacent monomer.
source: The second density located near the SBVS pocket appeared to be bound at the interface of the S4-S5 linker of one monomer and the S6 helix of an adjacent monomer (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The S4-S5 linker region of TRPV5 has a local resolution of 3.0–3.5 Å which allowed for unambiguous side chain and backbone placement.
source: This region of TRPV5 has a local resolution of 3.0–3.5 Å which allowed for unambiguous side chain and backbone placement (Figure 3—figure supplements 3–4).
evidence: This is a statement about the quality of the structural data.

claim: The density at the S4-S5 linker, though present in the sharpened cryo-EM density map, was not consistently visible in the half-maps.
source: It should be noted that this density, though present in the sharpened cryo-EM density map, was not consistently visible in the half-maps and therefore could be attributed to either low occupancy inhibitor binding or noise (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is an observation about the quality and interpretation of the cryo-EM density.

claim: The M491A mutation of TRPV5 resulted in only a small decrease in the inhibitory potency of ZINC17988990 with an IC50 of 0.258 ± 0.093 μM.
source: We observed only a small decrease in the inhibitory potency of ZINC17988990 on this mutant (IC50 = 0.258 ± 0.093 μM; Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is experimental data from mutagenesis and dose-response experiments.

claim: Inhibition of the M491A-D406A double mutant by ZINC17988990 was indistinguishable from the D406A S1-S4 bundle mutant.
source: Furthermore, inhibition of the M491A-D406A double mutant by ZINC17988990 was indistinguishable from the D406A S1-S4 bundle mutant (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is experimental data from mutagenesis experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The S4-S5 linker is unlikely to play a major role in ZINC17988990-mediated inhibition.
source: These data show that the S4-S5 linker is unlikely to play a major role in ZINC17988990-mediated inhibition.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutagenesis data.

claim: The binding site of the PI(4,5)P2 head group does not overlap with the identified inhibitor binding site in the S1-S4 bundle.
source: The binding site of the PI(4,5)P2 head group, a well characterized endogenous activator of TRPV5, does not overlap with this identified inhibitor binding site, which implies that the mechanism of inhibition for this novel specific compound is not to directly compete for binding with PI(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the structures and an inference about mechanism.

claim: The mechanism of inhibition for ZINC17988990 is not to directly compete for binding with PI(4,5)P2.
source: The binding site of the PI(4,5)P2 head group, a well characterized endogenous activator of TRPV5, does not overlap with this identified inhibitor binding site, which implies that the mechanism of inhibition for this novel specific compound is not to directly compete for binding with PI(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observation that binding sites do not overlap.

claim: Conformational changes due to inhibitor binding could lock the channel in a state that would not allow for PI(4,5)P2-mediated activation.
source: Rather, it is possible that conformational changes due to inhibitor binding could lock the channel in a state that would not allow for PI(4,5)P2-mediated activation.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of inhibition based on structural observations.

claim: Large movements of the TRPV5 channel occur during PI(4,5)P2 induced channel opening.
source: Large movements of the TRPV5 channel have been shown to occur during PI(4,5)P2 induced channel opening (Hughes et al., 2018a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous structural work.

claim: The rearrangement of the lower S6 helix caused by the phosphate head group binding to R584 causes global shifts in the protein from the lipid-bound apo state to the opened PI(4,5)P2-bound state.
source: Specifically, the rearrangement of the lower S6 helix caused by the phosphate head group binding to R584 causes global shifts in the protein from the lipid-bound apo state (PDB: 6DMR) to the opened PI(4,5)P2-bound state (PDB: 6DMU).
evidence: This is a description of conformational changes observed in previous structures.

claim: The ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure is similar to the lipid-bound apo structure.
source: While the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure is similar to the lipid-bound apo structure, there are several key differences when comparing this inhibited state to the lipid-bound apo state.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the structures.

claim: The S1-S4 bundle of the ZINC17988990-bound structure appears to have undergone a shift from the lipid-bound apo structure to accommodate the binding of ZINC17988990.
source: In particular, when aligned based on the pore dimer (all atom alignment of M497-R584 of opposite chains using PyMOL) the S1-S4 bundle of the ZINC17988990-bound structure appears to have undergone a shift from the lipid-bound apo structure to accommodate the binding of ZINC17988990.
evidence: This is an observation from structural comparison.

claim: The S2 and S3 helices of the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 have moved toward the ZINC17988990 density, creating a tighter space within the intracellular section of the S1-S4 bundle compared to the lipid-bound apo TRPV5 structure.
source: Specifically, the S2 and S3 helices of the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 have moved toward the ZINC17988990 density, which creates a tighter space with in the intracellular section of the S1-S4 bundle compared to the lipid-bound apo TRPV5 structure (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an observation from structural comparison shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Residues E403, D406 and Y415 appear to move 1–2.5 Å to accommodate ZINC17988990 binding.
source: Residues E403, D406 and Y415 appear to move 1–2.5 Å (as measured at the Cα) to accommodate compound binding, while F468 and Y467 do not appear to undergo significant conformational rearrangement (<1 Å movement at the Cα; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is quantitative data from structural comparison shown in Figure 5B.

claim: F468 and Y467 do not appear to undergo significant conformational rearrangement upon ZINC17988990 binding (<1 Å movement at the Cα).
source: Residues E403, D406 and Y415 appear to move 1–2.5 Å (as measured at the Cα) to accommodate compound binding, while F468 and Y467 do not appear to undergo significant conformational rearrangement (<1 Å movement at the Cα; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is quantitative data from structural comparison shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Conformational changes undergone in the S1-S4 bundle upon PI(4,5)P2 binding include movement away from the pore axis of all four helices, with the largest movements in the lower halves of the S1 and S2 helices.
source: Conformational changes undergone in the S1-S4 bundle upon PI(4,5)P2 binding include movement away from the pore axis of all four helices, with the largest movements in the lower halves of the S1 and S2 helices (aligned as described above, Figure 5C–D).
evidence: This is an observation from structural comparison shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: A counterclockwise rotation of the S1-S4 bundle and a pivot of the TRP helix occur to accommodate the helix transition at the base of the ion conduction pore upon PI(4,5)P2 binding.
source: Additionally, a counterclockwise rotation of the bundle and a pivot of the TRP helix occur accommodate the helix transition at the base of the ion conduction pore (Figure 5C–D).
evidence: This is an observation from structural comparison shown in Figure 5C-D.

claim: The shifts and rotations necessary for PI(4,5)P2 activation would be limited by the interactions of ZINC17988990 with D406 and Y415.
source: Based on the positioning of the ZINC17988990 density, these shifts and rotations would be limited by the interactions of ZINC17988990 with D406 and Y415 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The stabilizing interactions of ZINC17988990 with D406 and Y415 could act to lock the inhibited conformation of the channel in place and not allow for the shifts in the S1-S4 bundle that are necessary for PI(4,5)P2 binding and subsequent activation.
source: These stabilizing interactions could act to lock this inhibited conformation of the channel in place and not allow for the shifts in the S1-S4 bundle that are necessary for PI(4,5)P2 binding and subsequent activation.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of inhibition based on structural observations.

claim: The D406A mutation slightly but significantly reduced the inhibition of TRPV5 evoked by decreasing PI(4,5)P2 using the voltage dependent lipid phosphatase drVSP.
source: Consistent with this idea, we found that the D406A mutation slightly, but significantly reduced the inhibition of TRPV5 evoked by decreasing PI(4,5)P2 using the voltage dependent lipid phosphatase drVSP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is experimental data from drVSP experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The selectivity of ZINC17988990 is not likely due to a difference in sequence in the S1-S4 bundle region between TRPV5 and TRPV6.
source: Specifically, a comparison of this region in TRPV5 and TRPV6 shows very high sequence homology and therefore the selectivity of ZINC17988990 is not likely due to a difference in sequence in this region (Figure 4—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence alignment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3A.

claim: The structural difference between TRPV5 and TRPV6 in the S1-S4 bundle region may play a role in the selectivity of ZINC17988990.
source: Rather, it appears that the structural difference between TRPV5 and TRPV6 in this region may play a role.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of selectivity based on structural observations.

claim: The 16 amino acid linker between the S2 and S3 helices of TRPV5 has consistently been resolved as a stable short helix.
source: The 16 amino acid linker between the S2 and S3 helices of TRPV5 has consistently been resolved as a stable short helix while in the many cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography structures of TRPV6, this linker has not been resolved (Singh et al., 2018; McGoldrick et al., 2018; Saotome et al., 2016) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing multiple structures cited in the text.

claim: In the many cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography structures of TRPV6, the S2-S3 linker has not been resolved.
source: The 16 amino acid linker between the S2 and S3 helices of TRPV5 has consistently been resolved as a stable short helix while in the many cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography structures of TRPV6, this linker has not been resolved (Singh et al., 2018; McGoldrick et al., 2018; Saotome et al., 2016) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing multiple structures cited in the text.

claim: The S2-S3 linker region is extremely flexible in TRPV6 while it is consistently more stable in TRPV5.
source: This implies that this region is extremely flexible in TRPV6 while it is consistently more stable in TRPV5 (Hughes et al., 2018a; Hughes et al., 2018b; Gao et al., 2016) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observations and citations.

claim: Both Y415 and D406 are unresolved in all reported TRPV6 structures.
source: Both Y415 and D406, which make contacts with the drug density in the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure, are unresolved in all reported TRPV6 structures.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing TRPV5 and TRPV6 structures.

claim: The lack of stability in the S2-S3 linker region in TRPV6 may not allow for Y415 and D406 to establish interactions with ZINC17988990, preventing effective inhibition.
source: The lack of stability in this region in TRPV6 may not allow for those residues to establish interactions with ZINC17988990, preventing effective inhibition.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of selectivity based on structural observations.

claim: The structural difference in the S2-S3 linker between TRPV5 and TRPV6 could be due to small differences in sequence in the regions that stabilize the S2-S3 linker in TRPV5, such as the TRP domain and the N-linker.
source: This structural difference could be due to small differences in sequence in the regions that stabilize the S2-S3 linker in TRPV5, such as the TRP domain and the N-linker.
evidence: This is speculation about the structural basis for the observed differences.

claim: In the ZINC9155420-bound TRPV5 structure, the density attributed to bound inhibitor is located at the interface between the S4-S5 linker of one monomer and the S6 helix of an adjacent monomer.
source: In the ZINC9155420-bound TRPV5 structure, the density attributed to bound inhibitor is located at the interface between the S4-S5 linker of one monomer and the S6 helix of an adjacent monomer (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 6.

claim: The local resolution of the S4-S5 linker region in the ZINC9155420-bound structure is ~3.5 Å which allowed for confident side chain and backbone placement.
source: The local resolution of this region is ~3.5 Å which has allowed for confident side chain and backbone placement (Figure 3—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: This is a statement about the quality of the structural data.

claim: The inhibitor density in the ZINC9155420-bound structure is found in both half maps and the sharpened density map.
source: This inhibitor density is found in both half maps and the sharpened density map of the ZINC9155420-bound structure and has not been seen in other TRPV5 cryo-EM structures to date (Hughes et al., 2018a; Hughes et al., 2018b; Dang et al., 2019) (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is an observation about the quality of the cryo-EM density and comparison to previous structures.

claim: Two additional densities appear to bracket the ZINC9155420 compound and have been assigned to lipid molecules which may be involved in compound binding.
source: Two additional densities appear to bracket the compound and, given their characteristic elongated shapes and their presence in previously reported TRPV5 cryo-EM structures (Hughes et al., 2018a; Dang et al., 2019), they have been assigned to lipid molecules which may be involved in compound binding (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cryo-EM density based on shape and comparison to previous structures.

claim: ZINC9155420 was purchased as a racemic mixture and therefore the functional and structural screens were not able to determine which of the stereoisomers exhibited the inhibitory effect.
source: ZINC9155420 was purchased as a racemic mixture and therefore the functional and structural screens were not able to determine which of the stereoisomers exhibited the inhibitory effect.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental limitations.

claim: At the resolution of the ZINC9155420-bound structure, the inhibitor density could accommodate multiple orientations of the compound.
source: Additionally, at this resolution the inhibitor density could accommodate multiple orientations of the compound, and limitations in docking scoring functions do not allow us to chose one over another.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the structural data and modeling.

claim: The low particle number (<5% of the initial particles) in the final ZINC9155420-bound TRPV5 structure was not due to problems of occupancy.
source: It should be noted that the low particle number (<5% of the initial particles) in the final ZINC9155420-bound TRPV5 structure was not due to problems of occupancy, as a density that we attributed to bound ZINC9155420 was present in the preliminary 3D refinement.
evidence: This is a statement about the data processing and interpretation.

claim: In the presence of ZINC9155420, TRPV5 may adopt multiple transition states which could have resulted in the small number of particles in the final structure.
source: It is possible that in the presence of ZINC9155420, TRPV5 adopts multiple transition states which could have resulted in the small number of particles in the final structure, though none of the classes discarded during processing were of high enough resolution to clearly identify alternative states.
evidence: This is speculation about the reason for the low particle number.

claim: The M491A mutation of TRPV5 resulted in a right shift of the ZINC9155420 inhibition curve with an IC50 of 9.08 ± 1.45 μM.
source: This mutation resulted in a right shift of the inhibition curve (IC50 = 9.08 ± 1.45 μM) which suggests that M491 on the S4-S5 linker is involved in ZINC9155420 binding and inhibition.
evidence: This is experimental data from mutagenesis and dose-response experiments.

claim: M491 on the S4-S5 linker is involved in ZINC9155420 binding and inhibition.
source: This mutation resulted in a right shift of the inhibition curve (IC50 = 9.08 ± 1.45 μM) which suggests that M491 on the S4-S5 linker is involved in ZINC9155420 binding and inhibition.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutagenesis data.

claim: The lack of selectivity of ZINC9155420 may be due to the extremely high level of sequence homology of the S4-S5 linker region between TRP family channels.
source: The lack of selectivity of ZINC9155420 may be due to the extremely high level of sequence homology of this region between TRP family channels (Figure 4—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is speculation based on sequence alignment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The S4-S5 linker has been shown to be critical for gating of several TRP channels and may be evolutionarily conserved due to its essential role in channel function.
source: This S4-S5 linker has been shown to be critical for gating of several TRP channels and may be evolutionarily conserved due to its essential role in channel function (Hofmann et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and represents an inference about evolutionary conservation.

claim: In the ZINC9155420-bound TRPV5 structure, the S1-S4 bundle appears to be occupied by a lipid as seen in other TRPV channel structures.
source: Unlike the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure, the S1-S4 bundle appears to be occupied by a lipid as seen in other TRPV channel structures (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structure and comparison to other structures.

claim: The D406A mutation caused a small left shift of the inhibition curve for ZINC9155420 with an IC50 of 1.52 ± 0.38 μM.
source: As mentioned earlier, we tested the effect of ZINC9155420 on the D406A mutant of TRPV5 in the S1-S4 bundle binding site; this mutation caused a small left shift of the inhibition curve for ZINC9155420 (IC50 = 1.52 ± 0.38 μM, Figure 4D).
evidence: This is experimental data from mutagenesis and dose-response experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The S1-S4 binding site is unlikely to be involved in ZINC9155420 inhibition of TRPV5.
source: This implies that this S1-S4 binding site is unlikely to be involved in ZINC9155420 inhibition of TRPV5.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutagenesis data.

claim: Neither inhibitor characterized in this investigation appeared to bind at the econazole binding pocket, originally used as the site for the SBVS study.
source: Neither inhibitor characterized in this investigation appeared to bind at the econazole binding pocket, originally used as the site for the SBVS study.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structures.

claim: There are no residues that overlap between the econazole pocket and the cryo-EM attributed binding sites (within 4.5 Å of docked poses at the econazole binding site).
source: Though this S4-S5 binding site is near the econazole pocket there are no residues that overlap with the cryo-EM attributed binding sites (within 4.5 Å of docked poses at the econazole binding site, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is quantitative data from structural comparison shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In both inhibitor-bound structures, the econazole pocket appears to be occupied by a tightly bound lipid molecule.
source: Rather, in both inhibitor-bound structures, this econazole pocket appears to be occupied by a tightly bound lipid molecule.
evidence: This is an observation from the cryo-EM structures.

claim: The density in the inhibitor-bound TRPV5 structures at the econazole pocket appears to closely resemble in size and shape the lipid density in the lipid-bound TRPV5 structure rather than the econazole density seen in the econazole-bound TRPV5 structure.
source: This density in the inhibitor-bound TRPV5 structures appears to closely resemble in size and shape the lipid density in the lipid-bound TRPV5 structure rather than the econazole density seen in the econazole-bound TRPV5 structure.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing the cryo-EM densities.

claim: The competition between a lipid and econazole for the site used for SBVS was unexpected.
source: The competition between a lipid and econazole for the site we utilized for SBVS was unexpected.
evidence: This is a statement about the unexpected nature of the findings.

claim: A post hoc SBVS screen using the ZINC9155420-bound TRPV5 cryo-EM atomic model identified ZINC9155420 and ZINC17988990 among the top-scored compounds.
source: Notably, a post hoc SBVS screen using (a) the ZINC9155420-bound TRPV5 cryo-EM atomic model with a lipid molecule in the econazole pocket and the other identified lipid in the vicinity, (b) the same ZINC15 compound library we used in the original screen, and (c) a screening grid centered on ZINC9155420, identified ZINC9155420 and ZINC17988990, as well as other derivatives of these two molecules, among the top-scored compounds.
evidence: This is data from a retrospective virtual screening experiment.

claim: The retrospective identification of the same novel TRPV5 inhibitors using the correct binding pocket gives confidence in the SBVS approach used.
source: Therefore, while SBVS protocols utilize predefined binding sites, and we did not foresee lipid occupancy of the initially used econazole site, the retrospective identification of the same novel TRPV5 inhibitors characterized here if one used the correct binding pocket gives confidence in the approach used.
evidence: This is an inference about the validity of the approach based on the retrospective analysis.

claim: ZINC17988990 is specific for TRPV5 over its close homologue TRPV6 as well as other TRP family channels.
source: One of these compounds, ZINC17988990 is specific for TRPV5 over its close homologue TRPV6 as well as other TRP family channels.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental findings from selectivity testing.

claim: ZINC17988990 inhibits TRPV5 with higher affinity and higher specificity than previously described compounds.
source: ZINC17988990 inhibits TRPV5 with higher affinity and higher specificity than previously described compounds, and therefore will be a highly valuable tool in future experiments to study TRPV5.
evidence: This is a comparison to previously described compounds and a statement about the utility of the new compound.

claim: ZINC17988990 will be a highly valuable tool in future experiments to study TRPV5.
source: ZINC17988990 inhibits TRPV5 with higher affinity and higher specificity than previously described compounds, and therefore will be a highly valuable tool in future experiments to study TRPV5.
evidence: This is speculation about the future utility of the compound.

claim: Two novel inhibitor binding sites for the TRPV5 channel were identified through structural and functional characterization.
source: Structural and functional characterization of two of these compounds identified two novel inhibitor binding sites for the TRPV5 channel.
evidence: This is a summary of the primary findings from the structural and functional studies.

claim: One binding site was identified at the interface between lipids, the S4-S5 linker of one monomer and the S6 helix of an adjacent monomer and appears to play a role in ZINC9155420-mediated inhibition.
source: One binding site was identified at the interface between lipids, the S4-S5 linker of one monomer and the S6 helix of an adjacent monomer and appears to play a role in ZINC9155420-mediated inhibition.
evidence: This is a summary of the structural and functional findings for ZINC9155420.

claim: The binding site identified in the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure occupies the intracellular half of the S1-S4 bundle.
source: The other site identified in the ZINC17988990-bound TRPV5 structure occupies the intracellular half of the S1-S4 bundle.
evidence: This is a summary of the structural findings for ZINC17988990.

claim: The S1-S4 bundle binding site in TRPV5 partially overlaps with modulators seen in the recent TRPM8 structures as well as the 2-APB binding site reported for TRPV6.
source: This binding site partially overlaps with modulators seen in the recent TRPM8 structures as well as the 2-APB binding site reported for TRPV6 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) (Yin et al., 2019; Singh et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies and reference to a figure.

claim: 2-APB is a small-molecule inhibitor of TRPV6 which acts as an activator for other TRPV subfamily channels while having no effect on TRPV5 function.
source: 2-APB is a small-molecule inhibitor of TRPV6 which acts as an activator for other TRPV subfamily channels while having no effect on TRPV5 function (Singh et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2004; Kovacs et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The specificity of both 2-APB and ZINC17988990 in spite of the high sequence homology in the S1-S4 pocket between TRPV5 and TRPV6 may be explained by the structural divergence of these channels in this region.
source: The specificity of both 2-APB and ZINC17988990 in spite of the high sequence homology in this pocket between TRPV5 and TRPV6 may be explained by the structural divergence of these channels in this region.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of selectivity based on structural observations.

claim: The binding of key residues such as D406 and Y415 in the S1-S4 pocket could limit movement in this region and confer inhibition.
source: Specifically, the binding of key residues such as D406 and Y415 in the S1-S4 pocket, that have not been seen to interact with any non-protein density in previous structures, could limit movement in this region and confer inhibition.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism of inhibition based on structural observations.

claim: The identification of a binding site that allows for specificity of TRPV5 over TRPV6 in spite of the high sequence homology now allows for a more controlled structure-based drug discovery effort at this pocket.
source: Moreover, the identification of a binding site that allows for specificity of TRPV5 over TRPV6 in spite of the high sequence homology now allows for a more controlled structure-based drug discovery effort at this pocket that has the potential to reveal additional specific small molecule modulators of TRPV5.
evidence: This is speculation about future drug discovery efforts based on the findings.

claim: This study has laid the groundwork for the development of more potent and specific inhibitors of TRPV5.
source: Overall, this study has laid the groundwork for the development of more potent and specific inhibitors of TRPV5.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the significance of the work.

claim: ZINC05626366 showed 73% inhibition of TRPV5 at 10 μM, but only 36% inhibition at 3 μM.
source: The other hit compound from the original screen, ZINC05626366, showed 73% inhibition of TRPV5 at 10 μM, but only 36% inhibition at 3 μM (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is experimental data from the electrophysiology screening shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: ZINC05626366 exhibited much lower potency than ZINC17988990.
source: Since this compound exhibited much lower potency than ZINC17988990, we have not characterized it further.
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental data and a statement about the decision not to pursue further characterization.

claim: 10 μM ZINC17988990 fully inhibited Ca2+ signals elicited by application of external Ca2+ in cells transfected with TRPV5.
source: We found 10 μM ZINC17988990 fully inhibited Ca2+ signals elicited by application of external Ca2+ in cells transfected with TRPV5, but it had no effect in cells expressing TRPV6 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B and H), consistent with our monovalent current data.
evidence: This is experimental data from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: 10 μM ZINC17988990 had no effect on Ca2+ signals in cells expressing TRPV6.
source: We found 10 μM ZINC17988990 fully inhibited Ca2+ signals elicited by application of external Ca2+ in cells transfected with TRPV5, but it had no effect in cells expressing TRPV6 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B and H), consistent with our monovalent current data.
evidence: This is experimental data from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ca2+ signals elicited by agonists of TRPV1, TRPM8, TRPM3 and TRPV4 were not inhibited by 10 μM ZINC17988990 in cells transfected with the respective channel.
source: Ca2+ signals elicited by agonists of TRPV1, TRPM8, TRPM3 and TRPV4 were not inhibited by 10 μM ZINC17988990 in cells transfected with the respective channel (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–H).
evidence: This is experimental data from calcium imaging experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The concentrations of ZINC17988990 required to achieve inhibition were higher in Xenopus oocytes (IC50 = 4.37 ± 0.69 μM) compared to HEK293 cells.
source: We also tested the effect of ZINC17988990 on rbTRPV5 expressed in Xenopus oocytes (Figure 2—figure supplement 3). Similar to our previous results with econazole (Hughes et al., 2018b), the concentrations required to achieve inhibition were higher in oocytes (IC50 = 4.37 ± 0.69 μM) compared to HEK293 cells.
evidence: This is experimental data from TEVC experiments in oocytes shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: ZINC17988990 did not induce any inhibition of hTRPV6 in Xenopus oocytes up to 30 μM.
source: As seen with our results in HEK cells, ZINC17988990 did not induce any inhibition of hTRPV6 in Xenopus oocytes up to 30 μM (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is experimental data from TEVC experiments in oocytes shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.
